title: Soft-reserve lanes + hosted contingency arbitrator for dedicated routing
creator: Aisha Thompson
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight arbitration layer that manages soft-reserve lanes (per-tenant, region-aware capacity reservations) and a hosted-contingency arbitrator that governs when and how requests spill from Dedicated pools to Hosted endpoints.

Motivation: Current dedicated->hosted spillover is brittle in bursty scenarios: tenants experience large latency variance and noisy preemption during region evacuations. We want deterministic, easy-to-inspect rules that prioritize SLO preservation, minimize quality regressions from variant demotion, and give platform teams clear levers (budgeted tokens, decay windows, and arbitration thresholds).

Scope:
- Soft-reserve lanes: ephemeral token buckets per-tenant per-region that reserve a small percentage of dedicated throughput for sudden bursts without immediate hosted spill. Configurable by tier.
- Contingency arbitrator: a policy engine that evaluates route decisions (dedicated vs hosted) using signals: live capacity headroom, SLO slack, recent variant quality deltas, and tenant burst budget.
- Variant demotion rules: when falling back to hosted, prefer nearest-quality model variant with deterministic demotion steps and forced sampling to monitor regressions.
- Observability: new dashboards and tracing tags showing arbitration decisions, budget burn rate, and per-request fallback reason.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict hard-reserve (guarantee) vs soft-reserve (best-effort): soft-reserve chosen to avoid underutilized dedicated capacity and to keep capacity auctions simple.
- Conservative fallback (high SLO preservation) vs aggressive fallback (lower latency but potential quality regressions): we bias to conservative defaults with tunable thresholds.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atl/confluence/display/INF/Soft-Reserve-Lanes-and-Arbitrator
- Prototype PR (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1448
- Incidence reference (previous outage analysis): https://redwood.incidents/2025-11-dedicated-throttle-postmortem
- Dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.local/d/3fa5r/arbitrator-playground

Open questions:
1) Default soft-reserve percentage by tier (P0: 10%, P1: 6%, P2: 3%) — do these numbers match capacity economics?
2) How to surface per-tenant budget exhaustion in Console without leaking noisy signals to users?
3) Expected billing alignment for tokens served from soft-reserve vs dedicated baseline?
acceptance_criteria: Soft-reserve lanes can be enabled per-tenant with tiered percentage and observed token accounting
Contingency arbitrator chooses dedicated when headroom > threshold and SLO slack positive
Hosted fallback occurs to predetermined model variant chain with at-least-one-sampled dedicated request for quality checks
Observability shows arbitration reason and budget metrics on Console dashboard
Canary rollout to 5% tenants in us-west-2 with detailed regression alarms
comments: 2026-03-03 — Aisha T.: Ran tabletop with SRE/Product. Consensus to implement soft-reserve as ephemeral token buckets rather than complex reservation tokens. Action: Marcus to prototype arbitration scoring function.

2026-03-05 — Marcus L.: Prototype of arbitrator merged to feature branch. Basic scoring uses headroom, recent p50/p95 latency deltas, and daily budget remaining. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1448

2026-03-07 — Priya Kapoor (PM): Reviewed behavior matrix; requested adding explicit reason codes for Console ('budget_exhausted','region_unavailable','preemptive_demote','slo_risk'). Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-09 — Design review (Sofia P.): Recommended UI copy for tenant-facing notice and suggested a 'grace window' indicator so users know when soft-reserve will re-fill. Linked mockups: https://drive.redwood/soft-reserve-mocks

2026-03-11 — Marcus L.: Load test notes — with 15% soft-reserve in us-west-2, 95th tail latency improved for bursty tenants by ~22% vs immediate hosted spill. Observed slight increase in dedicated queue depth; will add conservative autoscale triggers.
2026-03-12 — Aisha T.: Decided to default to P1 tiers = 6% soft-reserve. Security review not required. Preparing canary plan for release routing-2.3.
